newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent drifts from highs in tentative market.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent drifts from highs in tentative market.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures partially held on to their morning rise, but began to drift downwards in light trade Friday afternoon after bumping against mild resistance, brokers said.
January Brent was trading up 17 cents at $23.30 at 1550 GMT, off its intraday high of $23.54.
"Brent seems to have found some resistance and has gone very, very quiet for the moment," one broker said.
Brokers pegged resistance at $23.65 to $23.70, but did not think the market was likely to test that level.
December gas oil was up $3.75 at $222.75 a tonne
They said the market looked directionless and likely to hold steady in the near term, waiting for news to push it one way or the other.
"The cold weather and low stocks have largely run their course for the moment," one broker said.
However, another broker said: "There's no reason for this thing to go lower for the time being," a broker said. "It's holding steady."
Brokers said the sub-normal temperatures, particularly in the northern United States, made the market hesitant to go short.
"Would you want to be short in this market?" asked a broker.
